# Executed scope and interpretation

This package connects an actual order/address acquisition boundary to full signed native correlation queries, and proves/executes a conditional leading-zero contraction. All new science is author-run, shared-context and not formally admitted. General efficient QFT/Shor dequantization remains open.

## Order and address costs are real

For n=ceil(log2 N), n actual squarings remove the two-primary part of the unit order. A bounded first-return walk of the resulting generator discovers its odd order q; a paid binary power and first repeated-square return recover s and R=2^s q. An exhausted budget gives PARTIAL, never a fabricated order. The modular-action bound is O(q+log N), before full native bit/setup/verification costs.

Target recovery projects to the q and 2^s components, performs a paid q-cycle search and bit lifting, uses actual typed CRT arithmetic, then checks b^r=z. Its straightforward modular-action bound is O(q+s^2+log N), again before complete implementation costs. Precise coprime projected equalities already imply membership by Bezout even in a noncyclic ambient unit group; the executed final check is an additional implementation check. All fresh certificate replays are charged. Each request can return a proved nonmember or retain a failed/partial attempt without obstructing other research.

The first target checker stopped because its proposed negative test assigned an already-zero CRT field to zero. The unchanged implementation correctly accepted that unchanged certificate. INITIAL_CHECKER_FAILURE.json preserves this checker error; the corrected nontrivial mutation was rejected on the successful full declared run. This was not an algorithm repair or a hidden failed scientific example.

## Exact counting replaces repeated identity prefixes

With K initial zero readouts, ell=i-K, P=2^ell and H=2^K, the actual signed carrier vector depends only on the suffix x in n=PA+x. Let g=gcd(P,R)=2^min(ell,s), M=R/g and A0=P/g. For each |d|<P, incompatible r-d modulo g has weight zero. Otherwise rho=A0^(-1)((r-d)/g) modulo M; M=1 is handled explicitly. Writing H=vM+u gives

    W_d = M v^2 + 2vu + max(0,u-rho) + max(0,u-(M-rho)),
    Gamma_h(b^r) = 4^-K sum_d W_d C_suffix(d).

All modular/count arithmetic uses the actual typed implementation. Every matrix-entry product and sum uses the signed native observer. The suffix executor uses the same admitted carrier and phase bank, while the original program depth and modular target remain bound to the full history. Nothing substitutes a shorter program's modular powers. Full residual entries, both matrix sides and chronological gate order survive.

The existing carry coefficient includes 4^-ell; the new sum divides by 4^K exactly once. K=0 is a valid no-gain fallback. ell=0, s greater than depth, ell below/equal/above s, q=1 and M=1 with g>1 are covered. No conditioning on a zero-mass history is performed.

## Actual bounded checks

The two aggregation runs use the saved actual bank and full D61 phase-word admission before its certified exact D6 boundary codec. They compare all matrix entries with independent complete typed alias discovery followed by the previous two-carry coefficients. The main run has 12 complete-matrix cases, a unit nonmember and a nonunit zero case, plus seven negative controls. A separate run adds two K=0 complete-matrix cases with nonzero residual support. The new production sources did not change between or during these runs.

| Run | Cases / controls | Actual native core calls | Raw bytes | gzip bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Paid aggregation | 14 / 7 | 901 | 43,453,949 | 2,342,391 |
| K=0 boundary | 2 / 0 | 716 | 4,478,985 | 166,480 |

The main raw SHA-256 is `eb566ed690aed646988ed72bb4df1ccd9ff788bf75bea751e0100dc9b5f39b62`; the boundary raw SHA-256 is `289d5d09041187a72bbff80eec0c65811cacf56dc1a9480cc8e5be2297efc96b`. The corresponding summaries list every exact source hash, fixture, matrix equality and cost. Order/address unit checks have their own full payloads, source hashes, setup and digit replay costs; native core cache hits do not make replay work free.

Cost review found that the first adapter replayed the inherited permutation before validating a supplied target certificate, losing that inherited receipt on three rejected targets. The final adapter validates the target first, so those rejected paths no longer perform the omitted operation. Both declared aggregation checks were rerun successfully with final adapter SHA-256 `ff7cf4c32d5cd86c68a2602c4991972004762343ecff4de72e735441b1a68768`. The old source, full raw evidence and summaries remain in aggregation/prior_validation_run; its missing receipts are explicitly a prior-run limitation, not reconstructed observations. The arithmetic formulas and all positive matrix results are unchanged.

## What improved and what did not

The O(R) full-cycle prerequisite of the earlier aggregator has been replaced by actual small-odd-part discovery and target recovery. This reduces a structural prerequisite when q is small relative to R. It does not necessarily reduce total work in a small example: new setup and certificate replays may dominate. See period_discovery/ODD_PART_DISCOVERY_NOTE.md and target_address/END_TO_END_COST_AUDIT.md for the paid comparison.

The counted suffix is also conditional. For N=65, a=3, depth 4, history 0011, targets 1 and 3, phase vector actions are respectively 24 and 30 versus 72 and 72 for independent alias summation; ordinary residue aggregation uses 24 and 24. For N=21, a=2, history 0101, counted suffix actions are 276 and 300 versus ordinary residue aggregation 96 and 96. Thus it is not a universal replacement even before address and integer-count overhead. These are action counts, not runtime speedup factors. Timing is bounded author-run observation, not an asymptotic benchmark.

For a long zero prefix its probability is Count(H,M,0)/H^2, which can be small. The actual all-zero weighted cyclic matrix can have full rank q while each entry has a short count formula. This rules out inferring uniformly low cyclic rank from the small carrier, but also rules out treating that rank as a universal computational lower bound. A proposed short common-root realization fails for a frozen actual noncommuting phase pair; the note states its exact limited scope.

Prior-art comparison and the classical same-information baseline are mandatory interpretation: learned order information can also feed classical postprocessing. No hidden order oracle, ignored bit growth, renamed q-point transform, or unmeasured rare-history assumption closes Shor here.
